subject: Anthropology
title: Structural Violence
description: A short lesson to help you apply Structural Violence.

hook.text: No one pulled a trigger. But poverty, racism, and neglect killed just as surely. This is structural violence.

buildup.text: Structural violence is harm caused by social structures — inequality, racism, and poverty — rather than direct force.

discovery.text: Paul Farmer coined the term to explain why the poor get sick and die at higher rates than the wealthy everywhere.

twist.text: It's invisible violence. No one is punished because the harm is built into normal systems — housing, wages, healthcare.

climax.text: Structural violence shows that health outcomes reflect social justice. Where you're born predicts when you'll die.

punchline.text: The deadliest violence is built into systems.

quiz.question: What is structural violence?
options: Harm caused by social structures like poverty and inequality

details.summary: Structural violence describes how social structures — poverty, racism, gender inequality — cause suffering and death as effectively as physical violence. Paul Farmer used this concept to explain why poor populations bear disproportionate disease burdens worldwide.
details.whyItMatters: Structural violence reframes health disparities as human rights violations rather than natural misfortune. It shifts responsibility from individual behavior to the social systems that create unequal access to health resources.
takeaways: Social structures cause suffering as effectively as direct violence
Poverty, racism, and inequality produce measurable health disparities
The concept reframes health disparities as systemic, not individual

faq.question: What is the relationship between poverty and disease?
faq.answer: Poverty creates conditions for disease through malnutrition, contaminated water, crowded housing, and lack of healthcare access. Poor populations are exposed to more pathogens and have fewer resources to treat illness. Poverty is not just correlated with disease — it causes it.

faq.question: How did Paul Farmer apply structural violence to health?
faq.answer: Farmer showed that TB, HIV, and other diseases concentrate among the poor not due to behavior but due to structural conditions. He argued that withholding effective treatment from populations because of cost is itself a form of violence enacted through economic structures.
